anomalies.observed: The Ethernet jack is only partially connected and its integrated-magnetics center taps are tied to module data signals: NET0008 joins U8 WAN_PORT_RX+ to J4 TCT, and NET0001 joins U8 LAN_PORT1_TX+ to J4 RCT. NET0017 joins U8 WAN_PORT_RX- to J4 RD+, while J4 RD- has no corresponding connection. The schematic also maps U8 WAN_PORT_TX+/- to J4 TD-/TD+ respectively.
anomalies.expected: Ethernet PHY differential signals should connect to the corresponding RJ45 magnetics data terminals as complete pairs; center-tap terminals should not be used as PHY data signals. The receive pair should not leave RD- open.

evidence.quote: U8 pin 3 WAN_PORT_RX+ is tagged NET0008; J4 TCT is tagged NET0008. U8 pin 5 LAN_PORT1_TX+ is tagged NET0001; J4 RCT is tagged NET0001. (SkylabModule sheet, page 2; EthernetAndPower sheet, page 4)
J4 labels include TD+, TCT, TD-, RD+, RCT, and RD-; the displayed NET labels connect TD+, TCT, TD-, RD+, and RCT, with no NET label shown on RD-. (EthernetAndPower sheet, page 4)
The module is described as having “1 WAN + 4 LAN 10/100 ports”; the open item notes that the RJ45 data pads are unconnected in the examined reference netlist. (§2 Component Table; §3 Open item)

anomalies.impact: The Ethernet interface is wired inconsistently with the PHY differential pairs: center taps carry data signals and the receive connection is incomplete. The jack is therefore unlikely to provide reliable Ethernet operation and may prevent link or data communication.

parsed.summary: The schematic connects Ethernet PHY data nets to integrated-magnetics center taps and leaves the receive pair incomplete. These connections are visible across the module and power-sheet drawings and are inconsistent with a usable 10/100 Ethernet interface.
